steps: Learn the key vocabulary for family members and physical descriptions
Master adjective agreement rules for gender and number
Use ser for personality and tener for hair and eyes
Practice building extended descriptions using connectives like pero and además
method_card.title: Family and Describing People
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family members, physical appearance and personality adjectives. You need to master adjective agreement (gender and number) and use ser for personality and tener for physical features.

SpanishEnglish
la madremother
el padrefather
el hermano / la hermanabrother / sister
el abuelo / la abuelagrandfather / grandmother
el primo / la primacousin (m/f)
el padrastro / la madrastrastepfather / stepmother
alto/atall
bajo/ashort
simpático/anice, friendly
gracioso/afunny
trabajador(a)hardworking
perezoso/alazy
Tiene el pelo largoHe/She has long hair
Tiene los ojos verdesHe/She has green eyes

Grammar focus: Adjectives ending in -o change to -a for feminine, -os for masculine plural, -as for feminine plural. Adjectives ending in -e (e.g. inteligente) only change for plural (inteligentes).

Model: Mi madre es alta y delgada con el pelo largo y moreno. Es muy simpática y trabajadora. (My mother is tall and slim with long dark hair. She is very nice and hardworking.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — family descriptions appear every year

gold.source_text: In my family there are five people. I live with my mother, my stepfather and my two brothers. My older brother is very funny but sometimes lazy.
model_answers: En mi familia somos cinco personas. Vivo con mi madre, mi padrastro y mis dos hermanos. Mi hermano mayor es muy gracioso pero a veces perezoso.

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish

distractor_labels.son: wrong number — son is plural (they are), but we need singular es (she is)
distractor_labels.está: wrong verb — use ser (es) for personality, not estar (está)
distractor_labels.estricto: wrong gender — abuela is feminine, so estricta not estricto

bullets.note: somos + number + personas (we are four people)
bullets.prompt: Say how many people there are in your family.
bullets.model_answer: En mi familia somos cuatro personas.

bullets.note: tener for physical features: tiene el pelo... y los ojos...
bullets.prompt: Describe your brother or sister's appearance.
bullets.model_answer: Mi hermana tiene el pelo largo y rubio y los ojos azules.

bullets.note: ser + adjective (with correct agreement) + connective + qualifier
bullets.prompt: Describe your brother or sister's personality.
bullets.model_answer: Es muy simpática y graciosa, pero a veces es un poco perezosa.

bullets.note: llevarse bien con + reason with porque
bullets.prompt: Say who you get on well with and why.
bullets.model_answer: Me llevo muy bien con mi madre porque es muy comprensiva y siempre me escucha.

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: En mi familia somos cinco personas. Mi madre es alta y tiene el pelo largo y moreno. Es muy simpática.
gold.translation: In my family there are five people. My mother is tall and has long dark hair. She is very nice.

wrong.generosas: generosas is feminine plural. Abuelos (mixed gender) takes masculine plural → generosos.

gaps.correct_explain: tolerantes — adjectives ending in -e just add -s for plural. No gender change needed.

wrong.estricto: estricto is singular. You need the plural form → estrictos.
wrong.estrictas: estrictas is feminine plural. Abuelos takes masculine plural → estrictos.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish family members to their English meaning
Match the Spanish adjectives to their English meaning

wrong.está: está is from estar, used for temporary states or locations, not personality traits.
wrong.tiene: tiene means 'has' — you need ser (to be) before an adjective like simpática.

gaps.correct_explain: es is the correct form of ser for describing personality — a permanent characteristic.

wrong.es: es means 'is' — in Spanish you say 'has the hair' (tiene el pelo), not 'is the hair'.
wrong.hay: hay means 'there is/are' and cannot be used to describe a person's features.

gaps.correct_explain: tiene (has) is used with physical features like hair and eyes in Spanish.

gaps.rule: Mayor/menor do not change for gender

wrong.viejo: viejo means 'old' (age), but for siblings you should use mayor (older).
wrong.grande: grande means 'big', not 'older'. Use mayor for older siblings.

gaps.correct_explain: mayor means older. It does NOT change for gender — it stays the same for masculine and feminine.

gaps.rule: Mayor/menor do not change for gender

wrong.menora: menora does not exist — menor never changes for gender.
wrong.pequeña: pequeña means 'small', not 'younger'. Use menor for younger siblings.

gaps.correct_explain: menor means younger. Like mayor, it does NOT change for gender.

wrong.es: es is singular (he/she). Mis hermanas is plural, so you need son.
wrong.están: están is from estar, not used for personality descriptions.

gaps.correct_explain: son is the ellas form of ser, needed for the plural subject mis hermanas.

wrong.simpático: simpático is masculine singular. Hermanas is feminine plural → simpáticas.

gaps.correct_explain: simpáticas agrees with hermanas (feminine plural): -a for feminine, -s for plural.

wrong.trabajador: trabajador is masculine singular. You need the feminine plural → trabajadoras.

gaps.correct_explain: trabajadoras agrees with hermanas. The irregular feminine of trabajador adds -a → trabajadora, then -s for plural.
